newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Rhone-Poulenc sees Greater China growth.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc sees Greater China growth.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc SA said on Tuesday it aimed to signifcantly expand its business and operations in the Asia-Pacific region, particularly in the Greater China markets of China, Hong Kong and Taiwan.

"We aim to achieve 15 percent of Rhone-Poulenc's turnover in Asia-Pacific by the year 2000, and double our sales in the region every five years," executive vice president Jean-Pierre Tirouflet said in a statement.
"Greater China will play an important role in the group's strategy. We expect total sales in Greater China will grow from US$250 million to US$1 billion by 2005," he said.

Asia-Pacific sales rose 20 percent to US$1.62 billion in 1996 over 1995, accounting for 10 percent of the group's turnover, the pharmaceutical and chemical giant said. The group has already invested US$800 million in the region.

"China will develop into a regional industrial base for Rhone-Poulenc in addition to the group's existing base of 12 industrial sites," Tirouflet said. "We expect half of our sales in China will derive from local production by the year 1999."
